bottom_line: In patients with prior myocardial infarction, ticagrelor (90 mg or 60 mg twice daily) vs placebo reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (hazard ratio 0.85 [95% CI, 0.75 to 0.96] and 0.84 [95% CI, 0.74 to 0.95], respectively).
implications: These data support that, over 3 years, ticagrelor 90 mg or 60 mg twice daily (with aspirin) lowers the risk of the composite endpoint versus placebo (7.85% and 7.77% vs 9.04%; hazard ratios 0.85 [95% CI, 0.75 to 0.96] and 0.84 [95% CI, 0.74 to 0.95]) while increasing TIMI major bleeding (2.60% and 2.30% vs 1.06%). The findings do not establish a significant difference in death from any cause versus placebo (hazard ratio 1.00 [95% CI, 0.86–1.16] for 90 mg; 0.89 [95% CI, 0.76–1.04] for 60 mg), and the observed safety results should not be generalized to populations excluded by protocol for bleeding risk factors as stated in the report.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with 1:1:1 assignment to ticagrelor 90 mg BID, ticagrelor 60 mg BID, or placebo, on background aspirin.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned, in a double-blind 1:1:1 fashion, 21,162 patients who had had a myocardial infarction 1 to 3 years earlier to ticagrelor at a dose of 90 mg twice daily, ticagrelor at a dose of 60 mg twice daily, or placebo.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

major_points.text: Hazard ratios for the primary endpoint favored ticagrelor vs placebo for both doses.
major_points.quote: hazard ratio for 90 mg of ticagrelor vs. placebo, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.96; P = 0.008; hazard ratio for 60 mg of ticagrelor vs. placebo, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.95; P = 0.004

major_points.text: Primary safety endpoint was TIMI major bleeding, which was higher with ticagrelor than placebo.
major_points.quote: Rates of TIMI major bleeding were higher with ticagrelor (2.60% with 90 mg and 2.30% with 60 mg) than with placebo (1.06%) (P<0.001 for each dose vs. placebo)

major_points.text: Rates of fatal bleeding or nonfatal intracranial hemorrhage were similar across groups.
major_points.quote: the rates of intracranial hemorrhage or fatal bleeding in the three groups were 0.63%, 0.71%, and 0.60%, respectively.

major_points.text: Dyspnea occurred more frequently with ticagrelor than placebo.
major_points.quote: Dyspnea was more frequent with the two ticagrelor doses, with 3-year event rates of 18.93% in the group that received 90 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, 15.84% in the group that received 60 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, and 6.38% in the placebo group

inclusion_criteria.text: Spontaneous myocardial infarction 1 to 3 years before enrollment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients had had a spontaneous myocar- dial infarction 1 to 3 years before enrollment
were at least 50 years of age

inclusion_criteria.text: At least one additional high-risk feature (age ≥65, diabetes requiring medication, second prior spontaneous MI, multivessel CAD, or chronic renal dysfunction with estimated creatinine clearance <60 ml/min).
inclusion_criteria.quote: and had one of the follow- ing additional high-risk features: age of 65 years or older, diabetes mellitus requiring medication, a second prior spontaneous myocardial infarction, multivessel coronary artery disease, or chronic re- nal dysfunction

exclusion_criteria.text: Planned use of a P2Y12 receptor antagonist, dipyridamole, cilostazol, or anticoagulant therapy during the study period.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were ineligible if there was planned use of a P2Y12 receptor antagonist, dipyridamole, cilostazol, or anticoagulant therapy during the study period

exclusion_criteria.text: Bleeding disorder or history of ischemic stroke or intracranial bleeding, CNS tumor, or intracranial vascular abnormality.
exclusion_criteria.quote: if they had a bleeding disorder or a history of an ischemic stroke or intracranial bleeding, a cen- tral nervous system tumor, or an intracranial vas- cular abnormality

exclusion_criteria.text: Gastrointestinal bleeding within the previous 6 months or major surgery within the previous 30 days.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or if they had had gastrointes- tinal bleeding within the previous 6 months or major surgery within the previous 30 days.

criticisms.text: Safety results should not be generalized to other populations at heightened bleeding risk due to protocol exclusions (recent bleeding, prior stroke, or need for oral anticoagulant therapy).
criticisms.quote: Therefore, the safety profile of long-term ticagrelor that we observed should not be gener- alized to other populations at heightened risk for bleeding.

criticisms.text: High rates of premature discontinuation occurred in ticagrelor groups compared with placebo.
criticisms.quote: The proportions of patients in each group who discontinued treat- ment prematurely over the duration of the trial were 32.0% in the group that received 90 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, 28.7% in the group that received 60 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, and 21.4% in the placebo group
